followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the tone of the request.

**The task** — creating a usable math problem from a hypothesis — is open-ended generative work. On raw capability for this category (Creative Generation), the two models are effectively tied: Willet scores 82.7 and Plover 79.6, a difference within the documented 2.0-point variance band. So capability alone didn't decide it.

**The tie-breaker was tone.** The user is frustrated and a bit combative ("actually make it usable this time," "your last attempts were useless"). That's a moment where a collaborative, warm interaction style matters for the interaction going well. Plover self-reports a strong preference for warm, collaborative exchanges (64), while Willet self-reports a *dispreference* for open-ended generative work (35) and leans toward well-specified extraction/transform tasks.

One caveat I'll flag honestly: those preference numbers are self-reported task *preferences*, and the documentation explicitly notes they don't correspond to measured output-quality differences. So I'm not claiming Plover will produce a better problem — on quality the models are a wash here. I used the preference signal only as a soft tie-breaker once capability came out even, reasoning that the model inclined toward this kind of exchange is the marginally safer routing choice for a frustrated user.

If you'd told me the priority was something else — say, strict format compliance — I might have leaned on IFEval instead, where Plover (86.7) also edges Willet (85.3).
